![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/ccdbd48b6cdf40205fe15a0b52553926aa4ba5e66e5a29bcf9ce6ae4164154a4.png)

Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠v.$
question.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ and $∠3$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/50d1e010a8279bf8f59a5e57b4ee4d4b744af7e431351bb17397e123aa79c59a.png)

Note that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${100}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠2={100}^{∘}.
$$

Similarly, note that $∠3$ and the angle whose measure is ${36}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠3={36}^{∘}.
$$

Let's add these measures to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/ce9944a3fa28177bd0882fccd53d544159b6f041c570e7037cac7db31103130e.png)

The angles $∠v$, $∠2,$ and $∠3$ combined give a straight angle. So, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠v+m∠2+m∠3 & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠v+{100}^{∘}+{36}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠v+{136}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠v & ={44}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
